subsections.theoreticalFoundation:
## Why Multi-Command Chains (&) matters

In any AI-assisted development workflow, **ampersand** is not a nice-to-have — it is the difference between a toy demo and a tool you trust on real code. AXON treats this topic as first-class because developers repeat the same questions every session until the system encodes the answer once.

### Design principles

The Chained Agents & Commands chapter exists because AXON is **local-first**: your files, your terminal, your approval gates. That architecture pushes complexity to explicit, inspectable mechanisms rather than hidden platform magic. Understanding ampersand lets you predict what AXON will do before it does it.

### Mental model

Think of ampersand as a contract between you and the agent loop in `main.py` → `llm_client.py`. The contract defines inputs (your message, memory, skills), outputs (tool calls, streaming text), and failure boundaries (approval, timeout, token limits). When the contract is clear, debugging becomes mechanical instead of mystical.

### Further reading in this bible

Cross-link mentally to adjacent pages in this chapter and to the Reference Appendix (Chapter 15) for tables and schemas. The goal is cumulative knowledge: each page should make the next page faster to absorb.
subsections.markdown:
## Practical deep-dive: Multi-Command Chains (&)

This section walks through **ampersand** the way you would explain it to a teammate pairing on AXON for the first time. We cover the happy path, the files involved, and the observability hooks you can use to verify behavior.

### Step-by-step workflow

1. **Prepare context** — ensure `.env` has `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, project memory in `.axon/memory.md` mentions any conventions for ampersand.
2. **Invoke** — use the CLI prompt or Zenith dashboard; both route through the same bridge when connected.
3. **Observe** — watch terminal output for tool calls, approval prompts, and chain progress markers (`⛓` for multi-command).
4. **Verify** — check filesystem changes, git status, or Zenith chat history.
5. **Iterate** — capture repeatable flows as skills under `.axon/skills/`.

### Key source files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `main.py` | CLI loop, slash routing, approval UI |
| `llm_client.py` | OpenRouter agent loop, tool execution |
| `bridge.py` | WebSocket sync to Zenith (port 8765) |
| `skills_manager.py` | Skills + memory loading |
| `task_manager.py` | Plan/execute state |

### Tips for power users

- Combine with `&` chains when ampersand is one step in a longer pipeline.
- Prefer skills over repeating long natural-language instructions.
- Use `/cost` periodically during heavy sessions to track spend.

failureMode.title: When Multi-Command Chains (&) goes wrong
failureMode.markdown:
### Symptom

AXON hangs, returns empty output, or loops on ampersand without completing.

### Common causes

1. **Missing API key** — `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` not loaded from `.env`.
2. **Approval deadlock** — write/shell waiting for `y` but prompt scrolled away.
3. **Context overflow** — too many @ files attached; model truncates silently.
4. **Bridge desync** — Zenith connected but CLI restarted; refresh browser.
5. **Skill typo** — YAML `name` does not match folder or has invalid tools.

### Fix checklist

- Run `/clear` to reset conversation, keep memory.md.
- Check `python main.py` logs for stack traces.
- Verify port 8765 free: `netstat -an | findstr 8765` (Windows).
- Re-run with `/model` set to a stable default.
- Narrow task scope and retry one tool at a time.

examples.title: Minimal: Multi-Command Chains (&)
examples.markdown:
```text
# Smallest useful invocation for ampersand
User: demonstrate multi-command-amp
```

Expected: AXON explains steps, uses read-only tools first, asks before writes.

examples.title: With skill: multi-command-amp-helper
examples.markdown:
```markdown
---
name: multi-command-amp-helper
description: Automate ampersand
allowed-tools: read_file, execute_shell
---

Run context:
!`git status -sb`
```

Skill injects live git context before LLM instructions execute.

examples.title: Chained: plan then multi-command-amp
examples.markdown:
```text
/plan 'Improve ampersand' & /delegate reviewer Audit changes
```

Chain runs plan first, then delegates review to specialist agent.

examples.title: Failure recovery: Multi-Command Chains (&)
examples.markdown:
If approval denied, AXON stops the tool call and reports which step failed.

Re-run with narrower scope or pre-approve session for read-only shell.

examples.title: Zenith parity: Multi-Command Chains (&)
examples.markdown: Same prompt typed in Zenith web chat routes through `bridge.py` to identical handler in `main.py` — terminal and web stay in sync.

subsections.theoreticalFoundation:
## Why Quoting & in Arguments matters

In any AI-assisted development workflow, **quoting** is not a nice-to-have — it is the difference between a toy demo and a tool you trust on real code. AXON treats this topic as first-class because developers repeat the same questions every session until the system encodes the answer once.

### Design principles

The Chained Agents & Commands chapter exists because AXON is **local-first**: your files, your terminal, your approval gates. That architecture pushes complexity to explicit, inspectable mechanisms rather than hidden platform magic. Understanding quoting lets you predict what AXON will do before it does it.

### Mental model

Think of quoting as a contract between you and the agent loop in `main.py` → `llm_client.py`. The contract defines inputs (your message, memory, skills), outputs (tool calls, streaming text), and failure boundaries (approval, timeout, token limits). When the contract is clear, debugging becomes mechanical instead of mystical.

### Further reading in this bible

Cross-link mentally to adjacent pages in this chapter and to the Reference Appendix (Chapter 15) for tables and schemas. The goal is cumulative knowledge: each page should make the next page faster to absorb.
subsections.markdown:
## Practical deep-dive: Quoting & in Arguments

This section walks through **quoting** the way you would explain it to a teammate pairing on AXON for the first time. We cover the happy path, the files involved, and the observability hooks you can use to verify behavior.

### Step-by-step workflow

1. **Prepare context** — ensure `.env` has `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, project memory in `.axon/memory.md` mentions any conventions for quoting.
2. **Invoke** — use the CLI prompt or Zenith dashboard; both route through the same bridge when connected.
3. **Observe** — watch terminal output for tool calls, approval prompts, and chain progress markers (`⛓` for multi-command).
4. **Verify** — check filesystem changes, git status, or Zenith chat history.
5. **Iterate** — capture repeatable flows as skills under `.axon/skills/`.

### Key source files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `main.py` | CLI loop, slash routing, approval UI |
| `llm_client.py` | OpenRouter agent loop, tool execution |
| `bridge.py` | WebSocket sync to Zenith (port 8765) |
| `skills_manager.py` | Skills + memory loading |
| `task_manager.py` | Plan/execute state |

### Tips for power users

- Combine with `&` chains when quoting is one step in a longer pipeline.
- Prefer skills over repeating long natural-language instructions.
- Use `/cost` periodically during heavy sessions to track spend.

failureMode.title: When Quoting & in Arguments goes wrong
failureMode.markdown:
### Symptom

AXON hangs, returns empty output, or loops on quoting without completing.

### Common causes

1. **Missing API key** — `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` not loaded from `.env`.
2. **Approval deadlock** — write/shell waiting for `y` but prompt scrolled away.
3. **Context overflow** — too many @ files attached; model truncates silently.
4. **Bridge desync** — Zenith connected but CLI restarted; refresh browser.
5. **Skill typo** — YAML `name` does not match folder or has invalid tools.

### Fix checklist

- Run `/clear` to reset conversation, keep memory.md.
- Check `python main.py` logs for stack traces.
- Verify port 8765 free: `netstat -an | findstr 8765` (Windows).
- Re-run with `/model` set to a stable default.
- Narrow task scope and retry one tool at a time.
